raw.description:
Licensed Marriage and Family Therapist (LMFT) $62K-80K/yr

Position Requirement: Remote Full-Time and Part-time Positions Available

If you are looking for a new opportunity to grow with a clinician founded and clinician led organization, look no further! As an authentic, unique, and skilled counselor, you have a plethora of options when it comes to work. Hospitals, community clinics, investment bank funded group practice startups, state agencies, and more.

At OptiMindHealth, we continuously strive to provide consistent, high-quality care and expand the reach of mental health care services in our communities. Unfortunately, the need often outpaces the services available to those we serve and only adds to the current mental health crisis in our nation. To combat this crisis and further our mission, we need more compassionate and skilled clinicians to join our cause. We are not interested in the “burnt-out” clinician that no longer finds meaning in their work and is just going through the motions; we are seeking people with a passion to provide excellent care, and the belief that we, together, can make a difference. If that’s you, then you’re in the right place!

Our approach with our team is simple, we take care of you, the clinician, so you can take care of patients. How do we do that? By investing in your growth, supporting you financially, holistically, and professionally, while being flexible regarding your personal needs and goals. The work we do with patients is hard enough and over the years we have found that our team often does their best work when the administrative burdens are taken off their plate and they are able to be fully present with their patients. Our administrative support team handles all non-clinical tasks so that you don’t have to think about anything except focusing on your patients.

Why bother with the endless administrative burdens and isolation of private practice? Use your highly trained interpersonal skills to change the culture around mental health care, decrease stigma, and help people who need you, while being supported by an experienced multi-disciplinary team of clinicians. Let us take care of the rest!

Want to work part time? No problem. Want to do group therapy? Sure! Want to do long-term psychodynamic psychotherapy with all of your clients? We do it every day. Interested in treating couples? We can make that happen. Basically, what we are saying is that whatever outpatient care you are interested in providing, we can surely accommodate you. We know you have exceptional skills; we want you to be part of our team.

The perfect candidate will share our passion for improving and expanding access to high quality mental health care and will thrive in a culture that emphasizes creativity, authenticity, humor, compassion, acceptance, and determination. Telehealth or onsite, we support your authentic and unique growth trajectory, while being yourself and having some fun!

We prioritize the clinician's experience by offering excellent compensation, benefits, training/supervision, and flexibility. Whether you’re working from home or in one of our physical offices, if you’re doing it during your scheduled work hours, you’re getting paid for it. Our compensation packages include:

  • Starting Salary range: $62,000.00 - $80,000.00 per year.
  • 401K with maximum employee matching.
  • Health care benefits.
  • Generous paid vacation and sick leave time.
  • Paid administrative time for consultation, supervision, and documentation.
  • Full administrative support.

Here are a few extra perks our team loves:

  • Paid supervision, clinical rounds, and administrative time.
  • Customized schedules within available clinic hours.
  • Hybrid work environment if desired: Telehealth and/or in-person (in select locations).
  • Muti-disciplinary team approach to treatment.
  • Incredible administrative support team.
  • Company leadership that understands the practice of mental healthcare.
  • Inclusive, socially responsible, client focused leadership.
  • We are not a franchise or a big investor-backed company.
  • And most importantly, clinician-led and clinician-FOCUSED!

We know what it’s like to work in an organization led by businesspeople instead of clinicians. We, on the other hand, have organically grown as a socially responsible company that started as a single provider on a mission to destigmatize and broaden the reach of mental health care, to an integrated and holistic group of exceptional providers with diverse backgrounds working toward that mission. We are fortunate to have significantly increased the reach of mental health care services in our communities, and look forward to continuing to provide consistent, high-quality care to those we serve for many years to come.

We will rely on your expertise to:

  • Evaluate mental health conditions, diagnose, create, and implement a treatment plan, complete ongoing documentation including further diagnosis, treatment plan reviews, and case notes according to company policy.
  • Provide excellent care for clients and collaborate with a dynamic team to further the mission of filling gaps in our community.
  • Utilize creativity in interventions to help clients achieve and exceed goals.
  • Prepare and submit individual documentation for each session per company guidelines and protocol. 
  • For Full-Time status, clinicians must maintain at least 32 available hours for patient care per week.
  • Coordinate services with other care providers, families, work personnel, medical personnel, other OptiMindHealth staff, and school staff as needed.
  • Attend and participate in all clinical staff meetings and trainings.

Qualifications and Skill for This Positions: 

  • Master's degree in one of the behavioral sciences or related fields from an accredited college/university.
  • Full, current, unrestricted license to practice independently (LPC, LCSW, LMFT) is required.
  • Experience with electronic health records and completing clinical documentation.
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills.
  • Experience and willingness to work collaboratively and creatively to meet necessary deadlines.
  • Comfort and familiarity working with clients with a diverse range of problems or concerns. 
  • Ability to pass a background check in a way that confirms to us you can provide safe care.  
  • Demonstrate and model stable and appropriate boundaries with clients.

Additionally Valuable (but not essential) Qualifications for This Position: 

  • Experience working in community, group, or private practice mental health.
  • Currently paneled or credentialed with insurance network.
  • Multilingual or bilingual proficiency.
  • Specialty area of practice. 

We can’t wait to hear your story and look forward to sharing ours!

The specific statements shown in each section of this Job Description are not intended to be all-inclusive. They represent typical elements and criteria considered necessary to perform the job successfully. The job’s responsibilities/tasks may be modified and/or expanded over time. OMH will inform the employee when changes in the respective job description are made.

Salary: $62,000 – $80,000 / year

Psychiatric Nurse Practitioner (PMHNP-BC) $125k - $145k/year

Position Requirement: Full-Time

FLSA Status: Exempt

Location: Tuscaloosa, Alabama

Salary:

125K - 145K+

Work from Home! Competitive, negotiable salary! Work/life balance! Leadership and advancement opportunities!

Join a leading clinician-led behavioral health company today! OptiMindHealth (OMH) is expanding and seeking compassionate psychotherapists to join our team. Today, OMH provides superior behavioral health services to patients in Massachusetts and Colorado. Since 2016, we’ve specialized in serving both adult and adolescent patients in a supportive outpatient environment. Our practice strives to improve access to holistic and cost-effective mental health care while supporting our clinical staff in all aspects of their work. Our clinicians define this work as the perfect balance between flexibility and efficiency.

OMH offers a variety of part-time and/or full-time options to our clinicians. Packages can be customized towards every clinician’s needs. Packages can include some combination of:

· Competitive Salary

· Medical benefits

· Paid malpractice policy

· CEU reimbursement

· Paid time off (PTO) and paid holidays

· Productivity Bonuses in select areas

· Work-Life Balance

· Flexible Work Schedule

  • No extra on call work, simply cover the care for your own patients!

It is common for clinicians to diversify their work today. Therefore, OMH’s flexibility and part-time options are the perfect complement to your professional and/or personal commitments. You can feel secure that OMH will offer steady, consistent income throughout your tenure.

Work from or close to home:

With locations in Colorado and Massachusetts, OMH is continuing to expand into states around the country. OMH will work with you to identify the best “fit” and will provide everything you need to treat OMH patients remotely from the comfort of your home. Our interview process focuses on your skill sets, interest as well as geographic location to match you to the best available option to begin working with OMH. Ask to speak with our recruitment team today to identify the local office(s) in your area, as well as those offices that are being planned for launch. Of course, if you prefer to work from home, we also have fully remote positions available.

Responsibilities:

The Psychiatric Nurse Practitioner (PMHNP-BC) will participate in the integrated care team model at OMH. Outpatient behavioral health practices like OMH are getting more attention than ever before due to the emphasis on team approaches. Join OMH to perfect your skills in the emerging field of integrated behavioral health care. The interdisciplinary health care team includes physicians, psychiatric nurse practitioners, licensed clinical psychologists, and licensed mental health professionals (LCSW/LPC/LMFT/LMHC). OMH values clinical relationships between all provider levels and believes this coordinated, collaborative approach provides the highest level of care to the patients we are privileged to serve.

Customize the care for each patient:

Our clinicians have the unique ability to customize the care for each and every individual patient. You will have the autonomy to determine how often you see a patient as well as the appropriate length of time spent with each patient. Medication management and individual psychotherapy are the most common forms of clinical work performed at OMH, but our clinicians also perform family therapy, group therapy, and psychological testing as needed and/or appropriate to a wide range of presenting problems of our patients.

Pick your own schedule!

  • Enjoy the freedom to create your own custom schedules with the perfect work/life balance.
  • Typically, clinicians work between Mondays – Fridays somewhere between the hours of 7:00 AM – 7:00 PM.

Focus on the patient’s care without the hassle or any additional on-call responsibilities. Simply cover the care for you own patients! Our medical staff and clinical psychotherapists focus on the patient’s care and our back-office support team handles the rest. This allows our clinicians time to be spent where it should be; with the patients they serve. Each clinician is responsible for clinical care and documentation following treatment sessions. Once that’s complete, our support team will handle all billing, collections, credentialing, etc. Once you leave the office for the day, your time is yours. No additional on-call responsibilities and no time spent wasted dealing with insurance companies.

Interested in benefits?

Full-time clinicians are eligible for medical health benefits. Please speak with the recruitment team to obtain additional specifics on benefits.

Leadership & Advancement:

OMH is a growing, clinician-led company. Our Site Supervisors are geographically dispersed throughout the areas we work in order to have staff leaders available to every clinician. Talk with our recruitment team today about the advancement opportunities to become senior psychotherapists and/or site supervisors.

Licensure, Education & Experience:                                    

Licensure in Colorado and/or Massachusetts as a Psychiatric Nurse Practitioner with experience working with persons who have various behavioral health issues such as, mood disorders, anxiety disorders, personality disorders, substance misuse, and other psychiatric impairments under the supervision of a consulting psychiatrist(s).  We welcome new graduates!

Preferred: Successful completion of PMHNP-BC exam(s).

This document represents the major duties, responsibilities, and authorities of this job, and is not intended to be a complete list of all tasks and functions. Other duties may be assigned as well. 

Salary: $125,000 – $145,000 / year

raw.excerpt: Who We AreWe are a fast-growing vertical SaaS company leveraging innovation and disruptive technologies to improve consumer experiences, outcomes, and predictability within the plastic surgery industry.
raw.description:
Who We Are

We are a fast-growing vertical SaaS company leveraging innovation and disruptive technologies to improve consumer experiences, outcomes, and predictability within the plastic surgery industry. Our team thrives on challenges, embraces change, and is dedicated to transforming how the industry operates.

Our platform is what aesthetic medicine and plastic surgery practices run their business on, covering scheduling, clinical records, forms and consents, invoicing and payments, patient communications, and the marketing that sits in front of all of it. It is a multi-tenant platform holding millions of patient records under HIPAA and GDPR, and we onboard new practices every month.

While we are a remote-first company, we are currently only able to hire candidates located in the following U.S. states: CA, CO, FL, GA, IL, MN, OK, OR, PA, RI, TX, UT, and WA. We hope to expand to additional states in the future.

Who We’re Looking For

We are builders, and our managers build too. Leaders here write code, ship pull requests and review their team’s work every week, all the way up to the Head of Engineering. A manager owns a team’s outcomes from the first conversation to production: what ships, how well it works, and how the people who build it grow.

We build with AI as the default, and our managers lead it by doing it. You stay current on how the best teams engineer with AI, try new tools and practices in your own work first, and bring to your team the ones that earn their place.

As a Senior Software Engineering Manager you lead a product engineering team that works directly on the workflows our clinics run every day. You hire, coach and level engineers against a published bar, and you turn product intent into a plan the team believes in. You also take real work in the codebase: features, fixes and the hard reviews. Senior engineers follow you because they have seen your code.

Responsibilities

Leading the team

  • Lead a team of software engineers across time zones: one-on-ones, feedback, growth plans and performance conversations, held to the same bar for everyone.
  • Hire for the team and shape the hiring bar with the Head of Engineering.
  • Make quality the whole team’s job: reviews that teach, tests that mean something, and production behaviour the team watches as closely as its tickets.

Delivery

  • Own the team’s delivery from problem to production, including planning, estimation, risk and release readiness.
  • Partner with product management to shape work before it starts, so stories arrive clear and the team builds the right thing the first time.
  • Lead incident response for your team’s systems and make sure every incident leaves the platform safer than it found it.

Building with AI, and leading by example

  • Ship code yourself every week: features, fixes and improvements to the team’s tooling, built with coding agents.
  • Review the team’s pull requests and teach through them, holding AI-drafted work to the same bar as any other.
  • Stay current on AI engineering practice, test new tools and workflows in your own work, and roll out what proves itself to your team and across the organization.
  • Grow the engineers who will lead after you.

Requirements

  • 8+ years building production software, including 3+ years managing software engineers directly, with responsibility for hiring and performance.
  • You still write and ship production code as a manager, with C# and .NET experience.
  • Angular, PostgreSQL, Kubernetes and AWS are a strong plus.
  • Daily use of coding agents in your own engineering work, and experience rolling AI engineering practices out to a team.
  • Teams that built or operated systems under HIPAA, GDPR, SOC 2 or comparable regulation.
  • Experience leading distributed teams across time zones.
  • Written and spoken communication that works across time zones and with colleagues whose first language is not English. (Most of our engineers are in Latin America.)

Benefits

What We Offer

At Adoreal, we believe in supporting our team’s well-being and growth through comprehensive benefits and a collaborative, people-first culture. As a globally remote company, we prioritize flexibility, inclusivity, and teamwork rooted in the Adoreal principles.

Benefits & Perks:

  • Healthcare coverage for you and your family
  • 401k Plan
  • Paid time off (PTO) and paid holidays
  • Company equity opportunities
  • Fully remote work environment with flexible schedules
  • Collaborative and thriving team culture guided by Adoreal’s core values

Why Adoreal?

Joining Adoreal means becoming part of a high-performing, ambitious team that works hard, achieves extraordinary results, and enjoys the rewards that follow. Every employee receives equity, aligning us all in our shared success. Promotions and growth opportunities are limitless, driven only by your performance and dedication to our core principles:

In this role, you will act as a technical partner to customers and the regional Sales team, helping identify the right technologies, solve application challenges, and support successful product design-ins from the early concept stage through validation and production.


You will collaborate closely with Sales, Product Management, R&D, Quality, and other engineering teams to develop customer solutions, support new business opportunities, and share market and application insights.


This role is ideal for an engineer with a strong background in electrical engineering, power electronics, or related industrial technologies who enjoys solving technical challenges, working directly with customers, and learning across a broad portfolio of protection, sensing, control solutions. A power semiconductor background is considered a strong advantage. The successful candidate will be expected to support multiple Littelfuse technologies and engage with customers at both component and system level.


Key Responsibilities:


  • Develop a solid understanding of the broader Littelfuse portfolio and support customers in identifying complete system-level solutions incorporating multiple product families.
  • Provide technical support to customers throughout the application development and design-in process.
  • Analyze customer requirements and recommend appropriate technical solutions, working with internal product and engineering specialists.
  • Troubleshoot technical issues and support laboratory testing, validation, and investigation of application-related problems.
  • Partner with Sales to identify technical opportunities and support design wins in strategic customer projects.
  • Deliver technical presentations, workshops, and product training for customers and distribution partners.
  • Collaborate with Product Management, R&D, and Quality to communicate customer needs and contribute to product and technology development.
  • Monitor technical opportunities, support customer follow-up, and share application knowledge across the EMEA organization.
  • Travel across EMEA to support customer projects, technical meetings, and training activities.

About You:


  • Bachelor's degree or higher in Electrical Engineering, Electronic Engineering, Power Electronics, or a related engineering discipline.
  • At least 5-7 years of relevant engineering experience in Field Application Engineering, Application Engineering, Design Engineering, or a similar technical role.

  • Experience with power semiconductors is considered a strong advantage. Equivalent experience in power electronics, industrial automation, protection, sensing, or related application areas will also be considered
  • Ability to understand system architecture, technical specifications, and customer application requirements.

For this position, we offer a gross annual base salary of approximately €70,000 to €85,000 + bonus. The final compensation package will be determined based on your experience, qualifications, and technical expertise.

About the Workforce Intelligence Lab (WIL)

The Workforce Intelligence Lab (WIL) is an applied workforce research initiative. WIL builds methodology-transparent workforce intelligence, including labor demand signals, occupational and credential pathways, and training-to-employment outcome measures, and works with education, employer, research, and community partners to turn that evidence into grant and sponsored-project collaborations. Learn more:

Opportunity type: this is a contingent proposal opportunity in WIL's expert collaborator network, not a funded vacancy. It supports a competitive grant application WIL is preparing; no award has been made, and there is no guaranteed work or funding. If an award proceeds and the staffing model calls for it, WIL may offer a project-based contract or consulting engagement. We will ask before naming you or including your resume in any proposal.

What you'll do

  • Serve as principal investigator on criminal justice research and evaluation proposals
  • Design rigorous process, outcome, and impact evaluations of justice programs
  • Lead studies in priority areas such as drone-as-first-responder programs, gang and organized-crime interventions, and elder abuse and neglect

Apply to be considered.

Requirements

Required

  • Track record leading criminal justice research or program evaluations
  • Peer-reviewed publications or major evaluation reports in criminology or justice policy

Nice to have

  • Prior federal justice research award as PI or co-PI
  • Randomized or quasi-experimental evaluation experience

raw.description:
Licensed Marriage and Family Therapist (LMFT) $70K-85K/yr

Position Requirement: Remote Full-Time and Part-time Positions Available

If you are looking for a new opportunity to grow with a clinician founded and clinician led organization, look no further! As an authentic, unique, and skilled counselor, you have a plethora of options when it comes to work. Hospitals, community clinics, investment bank funded group practice startups, state agencies, and more.

At OptiMindHealth, we continuously strive to provide consistent, high-quality care and expand the reach of mental health care services in our communities. Unfortunately, the need often outpaces the services available to those we serve and only adds to the current mental health crisis in our nation. To combat this crisis and further our mission, we need more compassionate and skilled clinicians to join our cause. We are not interested in the “burnt-out” clinician that no longer finds meaning in their work and is just going through the motions; we are seeking people with a passion to provide excellent care, and the belief that we, together, can make a difference. If that’s you, then you’re in the right place!

Our approach with our team is simple, we take care of you, the clinician, so you can take care of patients. How do we do that? By investing in your growth, supporting you financially, holistically, and professionally, while being flexible regarding your personal needs and goals. The work we do with patients is hard enough and over the years we have found that our team often does their best work when the administrative burdens are taken off their plate and they are able to be fully present with their patients. Our administrative support team handles all non-clinical tasks so that you don’t have to think about anything except focusing on your patients.

Why bother with the endless administrative burdens and isolation of private practice? Use your highly trained interpersonal skills to change the culture around mental health care, decrease stigma, and help people who need you, while being supported by an experienced multi-disciplinary team of clinicians. Let us take care of the rest!

Want to work part time? No problem. Want to do group therapy? Sure! Want to do long-term psychodynamic psychotherapy with all of your clients? We do it every day. Interested in treating couples? We can make that happen. Basically, what we are saying is that whatever outpatient care you are interested in providing, we can surely accommodate you. We know you have exceptional skills; we want you to be part of our team.

The perfect candidate will share our passion for improving and expanding access to high quality mental health care and will thrive in a culture that emphasizes creativity, authenticity, humor, compassion, acceptance, and determination. Telehealth or onsite, we support your authentic and unique growth trajectory, while being yourself and having some fun!

We prioritize the clinician's experience by offering excellent compensation, benefits, training/supervision, and flexibility. Whether you’re working from home or in one of our physical offices, if you’re doing it during your scheduled work hours, you’re getting paid for it. Our compensation packages include:

  • Starting Salary range: $70,000.00 - $85,000.00 per year.
  • 401K with maximum employee matching.
  • Health care benefits.
  • Generous paid vacation and sick leave time.
  • Paid administrative time for consultation, supervision, and documentation.
  • Full administrative support.

Here are a few extra perks our team loves:

  • Paid supervision, clinical rounds, and administrative time.
  • Customized schedules within available clinic hours.
  • Hybrid work environment if desired: Telehealth and/or in-person (in select locations).
  • Muti-disciplinary team approach to treatment.
  • Incredible administrative support team.
  • Company leadership that understands the practice of mental healthcare.
  • Inclusive, socially responsible, client focused leadership.
  • We are not a franchise or a big investor-backed company.
  • And most importantly, clinician-led and clinician-FOCUSED!

We know what it’s like to work in an organization led by businesspeople instead of clinicians. We, on the other hand, have organically grown as a socially responsible company that started as a single provider on a mission to destigmatize and broaden the reach of mental health care, to an integrated and holistic group of exceptional providers with diverse backgrounds working toward that mission. We are fortunate to have significantly increased the reach of mental health care services in our communities, and look forward to continuing to provide consistent, high-quality care to those we serve for many years to come.

We will rely on your expertise to:

  • Evaluate mental health conditions, diagnose, create, and implement a treatment plan, complete ongoing documentation including further diagnosis, treatment plan reviews, and case notes according to company policy.
  • Provide excellent care for clients and collaborate with a dynamic team to further the mission of filling gaps in our community.
  • Utilize creativity in interventions to help clients achieve and exceed goals.
  • Prepare and submit individual documentation for each session per company guidelines and protocol. 
  • For Full-Time status, clinicians must maintain at least 32 available hours for patient care per week.
  • Coordinate services with other care providers, families, work personnel, medical personnel, other OptiMindHealth staff, and school staff as needed.
  • Attend and participate in all clinical staff meetings and trainings.

Qualifications and Skill for This Positions: 

  • Master's degree in one of the behavioral sciences or related fields from an accredited college/university.
  • Full, current, unrestricted license to practice independently (LMHC, LCSW, LMFT) is required.
  • Experience with electronic health records and completing clinical documentation.
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills.
  • Experience and willingness to work collaboratively and creatively to meet necessary deadlines.
  • Comfort and familiarity working with clients with a diverse range of problems or concerns. 
  • Ability to pass a background check in a way that confirms to us you can provide safe care.  
  • Demonstrate and model stable and appropriate boundaries with clients.

Additionally Valuable (but not essential) Qualifications for This Position: 

  • Experience working in community, group, or private practice mental health.
  • Currently paneled or credentialed with insurance network.
  • Multilingual or bilingual proficiency.
  • Specialty area of practice. 

We can’t wait to hear your story and look forward to sharing ours!

The specific statements shown in each section of this Job Description are not intended to be all-inclusive. They represent typical elements and criteria considered necessary to perform the job successfully. The job’s responsibilities/tasks may be modified and/or expanded over time. OMH will inform the employee when changes in the respective job description are made.

Salary: $70,000 – $85,000 / year

We are seeking a versatile, highly proactive, and articulate Virtual Medical Executive & Practice Administrative Assistant to serve as the primary operational partner to a solo physician running a growing Direct Primary Care (DPC) / Family Medicine practice (~127 patients). This is not a basic data entry or phone-reception role; it is a dynamic position for an autonomous professional who thrives wearing multiple hats across clinical administration, operations, research, and executive support.

Your immediate onboarding priority will be managing the end-to-end patient record data migration into Atlas MD EMR—transferring demographics, medical histories, medications, allergies, and clinical documents while auditing charts for completeness and flagging discrepancies. As the migration completes, you will transition into the physician’s trusted "right hand"—managing practice administration, streamlining clinic workflows, managing calendars, booking travel, and creating executive PowerPoint presentations.

Working Environment & Core Schedule

  • Role Title: Virtual Medical Executive & Practice Administrative Assistant
  • Practice Model: Direct Primary Care (DPC) / Family Medicine (Solo Physician)
  • Status: Full-Time (40 Hours / Week)
  • Schedule: Monday – Friday, 8:00 AM – 5:00 PM EST (Eastern Standard Time)
  • Core Technology Stack:Atlas MD EMR(Preferred, tech-savviness prioritized), RingCentral, Microsoft Office (PowerPoint, Excel) / Google Workspace
  • Primary Scope: EMR Data Migration, Clinical Practice Administration, Executive Support & Operations

Top 3 Daily Tasks

  1. EMR Data Migration & Chart Management (Immediate Priority): Transfer patient demographics, chart histories, medications, and records accurately into Atlas MD, auditing records for gaps and flagging clinical discrepancies for physician review.
  2. Practice Administration & Workflow Management: Manage patient scheduling, track administrative action items, chase missing documentation, and build/improve daily operational workflows.
  3. Executive & Business Support: Conduct research, create polished PowerPoint presentations, manage provider calendars, coordinate travel logistics, and drive practice expansion initiatives.

Core Responsibilities

  • Atlas MD Record Migration & Auditing: Execute meticulous chart migration from legacy files into Atlas MD, ensuring demographic accuracy, document attachment, and zero loss of patient history (without making clinical judgments or altering clinical data).
  • Direct Primary Care Practice Operations: Triage administrative patient communications, maintain scheduling rules, follow up on outstanding paperwork, and assist in implementing new practice management tools.
  • Executive Administrative Partnership: Manage the physician’s executive calendar, handle professional correspondence, organize travel itineraries, and track outstanding projects through to completion.
  • Research & Presentation Development: Conduct business/clinical research and synthesize findings into clean, executive-ready PowerPoint presentations, spreadsheets, and summary reports.
  • Process Improvement & Autonomy: Proactively identify practice bottlenecks, build standardized operating procedures (SOPs), and operate independently so projects are completed without micromanagement.

Requirements

  • U.S. Medical Administrative Experience: Proven background supporting a U.S. medical practice, with direct experience in EMR data entry, chart management, and administrative workflows.
  • Executive Assistant Capabilities: Strong comfort and willingness to handle EA responsibilities (calendar management, travel booking, research, and presentation creation) alongside medical admin duties.
  • Software & Tech Aptitude: Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office (especially PowerPoint and Excel) or Google Workspace, with the demonstrated ability to learn new software platforms rapidly.
  • English Fluency: Excellent written and verbal English communication skills with a polished, professional tone.
  • Detail Orientation & Initiative: High organizational skills, exceptional follow-through, and the ability to work independently with minimal oversight.
  • HIPAA Compliance: Solid understanding of HIPAA regulations and a commitment to protecting patient health information (PHI).
  • Remote Workspace: Dedicated, quiet, HIPAA-compliant home workspace equipped with a high-performance computer (PC/Mac), high-speed internet, backup power/internet solutions, and a noise-canceling headset.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with Atlas MD EMR, Direct Primary Care (DPC), or Family Medicine clinic workflows.
  • Hands-on experience with EMR record migration or mass data transfer projects.
  • Prior experience supporting a solo practitioner, business owner, or medical director as an Executive Assistant.
  • Familiarity with RingCentral or virtual telephony platforms.

Ideal Candidate Profile

You are equal parts medical admin, executive assistant, and operations coordinator. You master new software quickly, take full ownership of EMR chart migration, handle executive logistics seamlessly, and keep a growing Direct Primary Care practice running with precision.

raw.description:
Risk Model Engineer — Pipeline Integrity (Transmission)

Location: Remote (US or Canada)
Department: Insights (AI/ML)
Reports to: Data Science Team Lead

Risk Model Engineer – Oil & Gas Transmission

Opportunity

If you want your work to make infrastructure smarter, safer, and more resilient, you’ll thrive here.

Irth Solutions builds advanced technology that empowers the people who keep our lights on, water running, and pipelines flowing. Our tools enhance the safety, reliability, and efficiency of critical infrastructure and the field technicians, engineers, and analysts who operate it.

We’re building a new AI-driven threat and risk management platform for pipeline asset integrity, and we’re looking for a Risk Model Engineer to own the transmission risk models that power its analytical layer.

Operators already run our probabilistic threat models in production today. You’ll migrate these models to our new platform, validate them against existing implementations, extend coverage across the transmission threat landscape, and help build Irth’s own model library. Your work will produce risk assessments and reliability calculations that pipeline operators can explain, defend, and support under regulatory scrutiny.

The work spans physics-based probabilistic models and machine learning, with a focus on producing results that are technically sound, explainable, and defensible.

Practical experience in North American oil and gas transmission is our top priority. We encourage strong industry candidates to apply even if their modeling experience is less extensive. We’re hiring two engineers and will balance the team’s strengths, with one potentially bringing deeper industry expertise and the other deeper modeling expertise.

Location: Remote within the United States or Canada, with working hours within approximately four hours of Central Time.

What You’ll Do

  • Migrate existing probabilistic model code to the new risk management platform and validate results against the current production implementation.
  • Integrate model inputs from diverse datasets across Irth’s product offerings.
  • Extend threat coverage across transmission pipeline integrity domains, including corrosion, cracking, third-party damage, outside forces, and other relevant threats.
  • Design and build time-series, anomaly detection, and geospatial models using inspection, sensor, maintenance, and related data.
  • Implement industry-standard probabilistic risk models within the analytical layer and support customer-driven model development on the platform.
  • Develop, evaluate, and present robust sensitivity analyses for all model offerings.
  • Validate model outputs against customer data, known outcomes, and applicable regulatory expectations.
  • Partner daily with ML Ops and data engineering teams, who own productionization, while you own the model methodology, content, validation, and supporting evidence.

What Will Help You Succeed

We don’t expect one candidate to bring every skill or experience listed. Practical North American oil and gas transmission experience is our highest priority. We’re looking for a combination of industry knowledge, quantitative modeling expertise, and sound engineering judgment across the two hires.

  • Transmission pipeline integrity: Experience with pipeline integrity management, threat identification, risk assessment, and integrity mitigation or remediation prioritization.
  • Threat and failure mechanisms: Familiarity with transmission pipeline threats such as external and internal corrosion, cracking, third-party damage, and other relevant threats.
  • Probabilistic risk modeling: Experience developing, implementing, migrating, or validating probabilistic models used to assess pipeline integrity or asset risk.
  • Inspection and operational data: Familiarity with in-line inspection (ILI), pipeline inspection records, sensor data, maintenance histories, or related operational datasets.
  • Reliability and sensitivity analysis: Experience evaluating model assumptions, uncertainty, sensitivity, and the impact of risk factors on model outputs.
  • Regulatory and customer-facing work: Experience supporting regulatory reviews, integrity assessments, audits, or customer decisions with clear, defensible technical evidence.
  • Machine learning and analytics: Experience applying machine learning to physical asset data, including time-series analysis, anomaly detection, classification, survival analysis, or related methods.
  • Geospatial analysis: Experience with spatial data, GIS tools, or geospatial risk assessment.
  • Python and software engineering: Sound engineering practices, including testing, code review, reproducibility, and disciplined use of AI coding assistants.
  • Real-world data and model judgment: Comfort working with incomplete or inconsistent data and the ability to distinguish a defensible, validated model from one that simply produces a number.

You don’t need to check every box. Candidates with deep transmission industry experience or strong quantitative modeling expertise are encouraged to apply, particularly if they bring working familiarity with the other area.

Why This Role Matters

Your work will help pipeline operators better understand threats, quantify risk, and make defensible integrity management decisions. You’ll contribute to the evolution of models already used in production while helping establish the analytical foundation of a new AI-driven platform.

You’ll work at the intersection of pipeline engineering, probabilistic risk, machine learning, and software development, with a direct impact on the safety and reliability of critical energy infrastructure.

Work Location

This is a remote position open to candidates based in the United States or Canada, with working hours that overlap within approximately four hours of Central Time.

Requirements

What Will Help You Succeed

We don’t expect a single candidate to bring all of the experience listed below. North American oil and gas transmission experience is our highest priority. We’re hiring two engineers and will balance the team’s strengths across industry expertise and quantitative modeling. Candidates with deep practical industry experience or strong risk modeling expertise are encouraged to apply, provided they have working familiarity with the other area.

  • Transmission pipeline integrity and regulation: Experience with North American oil and gas transmission integrity management, including applicable standards and regulations such as ASME B31.8S, 49 CFR 192, CSA Z662, or equivalents.
  • Fitness-for-service and failure mechanisms: Familiarity with fitness-for-service and remaining-strength assessments, corrosion growth modeling, or fracture mechanics.
  • In-line inspection (ILI) data: Experience working with ILI vendor data formats, data alignment, anomaly classification, and feature disposition.
  • Consequence and location analysis: Experience with high-consequence areas, class-location analysis, or related pipeline risk assessment requirements.
  • Regulatory and audit support: Experience preparing technical documentation and validation evidence for regulatory review, audits, or other formal assessments.
  • Quantitative risk and reliability modeling: Experience building or validating risk, reliability, or failure models for physical infrastructure. Pipeline experience is ideal, but relevant experience with rail, structural, water, or utility assets can transfer well.
  • Probabilistic methods and uncertainty: Familiarity with Monte Carlo simulation, structural reliability, uncertainty quantification, or related probabilistic methods.
  • Machine learning and physical asset data: Experience applying machine learning to time-series, survival, anomaly detection, or classification problems involving physical asset data. Experience training and validating models on sparse, imbalanced failure events is particularly valuable. We’re especially interested in candidates who are strong in either machine learning or pipeline integrity and have working familiarity with the other.
  • Geospatial analysis: Experience with ArcGIS, PostGIS, linear referencing, or geospatial risk assessment.
  • Python and software engineering: Sound engineering practices, including testing, code review, reproducibility, and disciplined use of AI coding assistants.
  • Real-world data and model judgment: Comfort working with incomplete, inconsistent, and imperfect data, along with the judgment to distinguish a defensible, validated model from one that simply produces a number.

You don’t need to check every box. We value sound technical judgment, practical industry knowledge, and the ability to build or validate models whose results can be explained and defended. We’re particularly interested in candidates who bring deep transmission expertise or strong quantitative modeling skills and can collaborate effectively across both domains.

Benefits

Benefits

  • Competitive Salary – A competitive compensation package based on experience and qualifications.
  • Medical, Dental, and Vision Insurance – Comprehensive insurance coverage to support you and your family.
  • 401(k) Plan with Company Match.
  • Generous Paid Time Off (PTO) – Time off to support work-life balance and personal needs.
  • Company-Paid Holidays – Paid holidays throughout the year.
  • Flexible Work Options – Work-from-home opportunities are available, depending on role and business needs.
  • On-Call Compensation – Additional pay for eligible on-call shifts.

raw.description:
LBM Solutions Specialist

North America

About us

Founded in 1992, GenetiQ is a global software company delivering flexible business management solutions to independently owned businesses in the lumber and building materials industry.

Our innovative cloud ERP solution, GenetiQ, is purpose-built for dealers, retailers, wholesalers and distributors — providing the tools they need to grow, adapt and thrive.

As we continue to expand across North America, we are looking for people who understand the LBM industry from the inside: people who have worked with dealers, distributors, buying groups, legacy ERP products, operational teams and real-world business processes.

Executive summary

The Software Solutions Specialist is a senior customer-facing role designed to bring deep North American LBM knowledge directly into GenetiQ implementation projects.

This role is not a traditional implementation consultant position. It is a specialist role for someone who can lead from industry experience, challenge assumptions, guide customers through operational decisions, and ensure GenetiQ is implemented in a way that reflects how LBM businesses actually work.

The Software Solutions Specialist will work across customer projects, delivery teams, product teams and development teams to accelerate adoption, reduce implementation risk, and influence product direction through real project experience.

The role exists to ensure that GenetiQ is not simply configured for customers, but shaped around credible, practical and commercially relevant LBM operating models.

Role Definition

The Software Solutions Specialist acts as a practical bridge between the North American LBM market and GenetiQ's internal teams.

The role will be directly involved in GenetiQ implementation projects, using prior experience with LBM operations, legacy ERP products, business processes and customer workflows to help customers make better decisions and help GenetiQ deliver better outcomes.

The role has four primary objectives:

  1. Project leadership through industry expertise
    Lead and influence customer implementation projects from the perspective of real-world LBM operational knowledge.
  2. Customer outcome acceleration
    Help customers adopt proven processes, reduce unnecessary customization, and make confident decisions during discovery, design, validation and go-live readiness.
  3. Product influence through project evidence
    Identify where GenetiQ needs to evolve by surfacing functional gaps, usability friction, workflow challenges and recurring customer needs from live projects.
  4. Internal enablement
    Educate consultants, project managers, product owners and developers on North American LBM practices, legacy ERP behaviours and customer expectations.

Why this role matters

GenetiQ's success in North America depends on more than software capability. It depends on our ability to understand how LBM businesses really operate and to translate that understanding into successful implementations, better product decisions and stronger customer confidence.

Many customers will be moving from long-established legacy products. They will expect GenetiQ to understand their language, processes, operational pressures and industry norms.

The Software Solutions Specialist provides that credibility.

This role will help GenetiQ:

  • De-risk complex customer implementations.
  • Improve the quality of discovery and solution design.
  • Reduce rework caused by misunderstood operational requirements.
  • Help customers adopt best-practice LBM workflows.
  • Strengthen the link between project delivery and product development.
  • Build market credibility in the North American LBM sector.
  • Turn project learning into reusable templates, playbooks and product insight.

Core responsibilities

1. Customer project solution leadership

  • Act as a senior industry specialist on GenetiQ implementation projects.
  • Lead or support discovery sessions with customer executives, owners, managers and operational teams.
  • Translate customer requirements into practical LBM process designs.
  • Challenge customer requests where legacy habits may create unnecessary complexity.
  • Help customers understand how GenetiQ can support modern, scalable ways of working.
  • Support project teams during design, configuration, validation, testing and go-live readiness.~

2. LBM operational expertise

  • Bring practical knowledge of North American LBM operations into each project.
  • Advise on workflows across purchasing, inventory, pricing, contractor sales, dispatch, estimating, rebates, EDI, warehouse operations, branch management and multi-location distribution.
  • Understand how legacy ERP products have shaped customer expectations and ways of working.
  • Help identify where customers need process change, not just software configuration.
  • Provide informed guidance on industry norms, exceptions and commercially important workflows.

3. Product influence and functional feedback

  • Identify functional gaps, usability issues and workflow friction during implementation projects.
  • Work with Product and Development to explain the operational impact of customer requirements.
  • Help validate whether proposed solutions will work in real LBM environments.
  • Prioritize product feedback based on customer impact, repeatability and market relevance.
  • Contribute to product design discussions by bringing evidence from live projects.
  • Help ensure GenetiQ evolves in a way that is credible for the North American LBM market.

4. Delivery enablement

  • Support consultants and project managers with LBM-specific knowledge during project delivery.
  • Help standardize recommended processes and solution patterns.
  • Reduce ambiguity in discovery and design by providing practical industry interpretation.
  • Develop reusable templates, examples, workflows and implementation guidance.
  • Coach internal teams on how to handle LBM-specific customer scenarios.
  • Support onboarding of new team members by sharing industry and legacy product knowledge.

5. Customer and executive engagement

  • Build credibility with customer executives, owners and operational leaders.
  • Act as a trusted advisor during workshops, project reviews, steering meetings and escalation discussions.
  • Help customers make informed decisions where there are competing operational, technical and commercial priorities.
  • Represent GenetiQ as a knowledgeable LBM partner rather than a generic software provider.
  • Support strategic customers where operational misalignment or product uncertainty could put outcomes at risk.

6. Market and legacy product insight

  • Maintain awareness of North American LBM market trends, customer expectations and competitive pressures.
  • Bring informed knowledge of legacy ERP products and competitor ecosystems, including Epicor, BisTrack, Spruce, DMSi, Agility and related solutions.
  • Help GenetiQ understand what customers value, what they are used to, and where they are likely to resist change.
  • Feed market insight into delivery planning, product prioritization and internal enablement.

Required experience and characteristics

The ideal candidate will bring a strong blend of LBM industry knowledge, ERP experience, customer credibility and practical delivery judgement.

We are particularly interested in candidates who have experience in one or more of the following areas:

  • 10+ years working in or around the North American LBM industry.
  • Experience inside an LBM dealer, distributor, buying group, software vendor or ERP implementation environment.
  • Strong understanding of LBM workflows, including purchasing, inventory, pricing, dispatch, contractor sales, estimating, rebates, EDI and multi-branch operations.
  • Experience with legacy LBM ERP products or business management systems.
  • Ability to lead customer conversations with confidence and credibility.
  • Ability to simplify complex operational issues into clear decisions and practical actions.
  • Ability to influence internal teams without relying on hierarchy.
  • Strong communication skills across customers, consultants, developers, product teams and senior stakeholders.
  • A practical, outcome-focused mindset.
  • Willingness to be directly involved in customer implementation projects.

This role would suit someone who

  • Has deep LBM experience and wants to help shape the next generation of ERP for the industry.
  • Has worked with legacy ERP products and understands both their strengths and limitations.
  • Enjoys solving operational problems with customers.
  • Wants to influence product development through real customer projects.
  • Can bridge the gap between business process, software capability and customer outcomes.
  • Is credible with senior LBM stakeholders but also comfortable working hands-on with project teams.
  • Wants a role that is more strategic and influential than a traditional implementation consulting position.

What success looks like

Success in this role will be measured by the impact the Software Solutions Specialist has on customer outcomes, product relevance and internal capability.

Key success indicators include:

  • Customers feel understood and guided by someone who knows their industry.
  • Discovery and design phases become clearer, faster and more commercially grounded.
  • Project teams make better decisions because they have access to stronger LBM expertise.
  • Product and Development receive clearer, evidence-based feedback from live projects.
  • Reusable industry templates and solution patterns are created and adopted.
  • Customer implementations are de-risked through better operational alignment.
  • GenetiQ strengthens its credibility as a true North American LBM partner.

Benefits options

Our perfect fit ethos extends to our team, ensuring that our roles, environment, benefits and progression paths are geared toward professional and personal development.

In addition to an excellent compensation package, we offer a range of benefits, including:

  • Healthcare: medical, dental and vision.
  • Short & long term disability.
  • AD&D insurance.
  • 401K plan.
  • Employee assistance program.
  • GenetiQ wellness reimbursement.
  • PTO: 20 days per annum plus GenetiQ-observed holidays.
  • Flexible working to support better work-life balance.

It is the policy of GenetiQ to promote equal employment opportunities. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, race, color, ethnicity, age, national origin, citizenship, religion, physical or mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, pregnancy, family structure, marital status, ancestry, domestic partner status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, veteran or military status, or any other basis prohibited by law.

raw.description:
About the job Head of Accounting

RMA Group is a multi-sector organization with more than 9,000 employees and an operational presence in 17 countries. For 40 years, we have developed enduring partnerships to support the needs of our clients, underpinned by the core values of Innovation, Integrity and Endurance. Through its various businesses including RMA Automotive, Global Fleet Sales, Comin Asia and Express Food Group (EFG), RMA Group has established itself as the partner of choice for leading automotive, equipment, engineering services, and food brands in Southeast Asia and beyond.

Overview and purpose of the role

The Head of Accounting leads the day-to-day accounting operations of the business. The role ensures accurate and timely financial records, reliable inventory records and valuation, strong internal controls, and full compliance with statutory, tax and Group reporting requirements. It owns the general ledger, accounts payable and receivable, payroll accounting, fixed assets, inventory accounting and control, tax filings and the month-end and year-end close. It also builds a high-performing accounting team that supports the wider finance organisation across RMAC Group's divisions.

﻿﻿Key responsibilities:
1. Accounting Operations
  • Oversee the general ledger, accounts payable, accounts receivable, payroll accounting, fixed asset registers and inventory accounting.
  • Ensure the month-end and year-end close is accurate, complete and on time, with a published closing calendar and clear cut-off rules.
  • Review journal entries, accruals, prepayments and provisions, and approve non-routine entries.
  • Oversee revenue recognition, warranty and after-sales accounting, and the accounting for related-party and intercompany transactions.
2. Inventory Accounting and Control
  • Oversee inventory records for vehicles, spare parts, accessories and workshop stock across all locations.
  • Ensure accurate and timely recording of stock receipts, issues, transfers, returns and adjustments, with correct cut-off at period end.
  • Oversee the costing of inventory, including landed cost (freight, import duty, clearing and other direct costs), and ensure costs are correctly capitalised.
  • Ensure inventory is valued in line with accounting standards at the lower of cost and net realisable value, and review provisions for slow-moving, obsolete and damaged stock.
  • Plan and supervise periodic and year-end physical stock counts and cycle counts, investigate variances and approve adjustments within delegated authority.
  • Reconcile the inventory subledger to the general ledger every month, including goods received not invoiced, goods in transit and consignment or demo stock.
  • Monitor stock levels, ageing and turnover, and report slow-moving stock and excess inventory to management.
  • Ensure inventory controls are in place over warehouse access, stock movements, vehicle identification numbers and the safeguarding of stock.
  • Ensure three-way matching between purchase orders, goods receipts and supplier invoices so inventory and payables are recorded correctly.
  • Provide inventory data and analysis to support purchasing, pricing, gross profit review and working capital management.
3. Financial Reporting
  • Prepare financial statements and supporting schedules in line with applicable accounting standards (CIFRS) and RMA Group policies.
  • Provide accurate trial balances and accounting data to the Finance Manager and finance analysts for management reporting, budgeting and forecasting.
  • Prepare Group reporting submissions, intercompany confirmations and consolidation inputs, including elimination schedules and intercompany stock profit adjustments where applicable.
4. Reconciliations and Data Integrity
  • Review all balance sheet reconciliations (bank, AR, AP, inventory, fixed assets, intercompany, accruals) and resolve discrepancies promptly.
  • Ensure supplier statements are reconciled regularly and customer balances are confirmed and followed up.
  • Maintain the integrity of the chart of accounts, item master data, costing data and subledgers.
5. Tax and Statutory Compliance
  • Ensure timely and accurate preparation and filing of all tax returns (VAT, withholding tax, tax on income, salary tax, prepayment of tax) and other regulatory submissions.
  • Ensure import duties and taxes on inventory are correctly calculated, recorded and supported by customs documents.
  • Ensure payroll deductions and contributions, including NSSF, are correctly accounted for and remitted.
  • Monitor changes in tax law and regulation and update accounting practices accordingly.
  • Support tax audits and correspondence with the General Department of Taxation and other government bodies.
6. Internal Controls and Compliance
  • Design, implement and monitor internal controls over accounting and inventory transactions, including segregation of duties and approval limits.
  • Establish and maintain accounting policies, procedures and SOPs, and ensure compliance with company, Group and local requirements.
  • Strengthen the AP workflow (invoice receipt, three-way matching, approval, payment scheduling) so suppliers are paid accurately and on time.
  • Ensure proper document retention and audit trails.
7. Audit Coordination
  • Act as the primary contact for internal and external auditors.
  • Coordinate auditor attendance at stock counts and provide inventory valuation and provision workings.
  • Prepare audit schedules and supporting documents, respond to queries, and track the resolution of audit findings and management letter points.
8. Accounting Systems and Process Improvement
  • Maintain and improve accounting systems, templates and workflows.
  • Work with the IT department on Odoo accounting and inventory configuration (including costing methods, stock valuation and warehouse workflows), raising clear fix, improvement and new-development requests, and testing the results before release.
  • Identify opportunities to automate and streamline accounting processes and shorten the close.
9. Team Leadership and Development
  • Supervise, train, coach and develop accounting staff, including those handling inventory.
  • Allocate workload, set deadlines and review the quality of team output.
  • Plan team coverage and cross-training so critical tasks never depend on one person.
10. Support to Finance Management
  • Support budgeting, forecasting and management reporting with timely and accurate accounting and inventory data.
  • Partner with the Finance Manager and CFO on ad hoc financial analysis and special projects.
11. Cost Control and Efficiency
  • Monitor accounting-related costs and inventory losses and write-offs, and identify efficiency gains.
  • Promote best practice to improve the accuracy and turnaround time of accounting deliverables.
HR Responsibilities
  • Support the development and implementation of HR policies and procedures affecting the accounting team, including onboarding, performance management and training plans.
  • Prepare HR-related reports for the accounting function as the company requires.
  • Report functionally to the Finance Manager and CFO on accounting team matters.
Financial Responsibilities
  • Assist the Finance Manager and CFO in preparing the annual accounting budget and monitor departmental expenditure.
  • Review and approve routine accounting expenditure proposals and inventory adjustments within delegated authority, ensuring compliance with Group and legal requirements.
Background and experience:
  • Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance or a related field. ACCA, CPA or equivalent is preferred.
  • Minimum 5 to 7 years of progressive accounting experience, including at least 2 years in a supervisory or team-lead role.
  • Proven experience managing full-cycle accounting operations and the month-end and year-end close.
  • Hands-on experience with inventory accounting, costing, stock counts and inventory controls.
  • Experience in automotive, distribution, trading or a similar multi-entity group environment is an advantage.
  • Strong knowledge of accounting principles and reporting standards (CIFRS, IFRS, including inventory standards), Cambodian tax regulations and statutory obligations.
  • Understanding of internal control systems, segregation of duties and audit procedures.
  • Knowledge of payroll accounting, fixed assets, inventory costing and valuation, and intercompany and consolidation accounting.
  • Proficiency in ERP and accounting software (Odoo preferred, including its inventory module) and advanced Microsoft Excel.
  • Excellent analytical, organisational and problem-solving skills.
  • Strong supervisory, interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to explain accounting and inventory matters to non-finance colleagues.
  • Good written and spoken English.
  • Strategic thinking
  • Sound decision making
  • Mentoring, coaching and performance management
  • Flexibility and the ability to work under closing pressure
  • High integrity and confidentiality

If you're interested, please send your CV to:

  • Email:
  • Telegram HR Contact Person:
  • Contact HR at: 070 790 890

﻿RMA Group is an equal opportunity employer, with a diverse group of colleagues globally representing different cultures, backgrounds, and beliefs. Our values of Innovation, Integrity and Endurance are embedded in what we do, and we welcome applicants who are committed to respecting diversity of thought, and in living our values on a day-to-day basis.

raw.title: Senior IT Security Auditor
raw.excerpt: About APTNEXUS Since our founding 2012, APTNEXUS has empowered federal agencies and commercial enterprises to navigate the complexities of the digital landscape.
raw.description:
About APTNEXUS

Since our founding 2012, APTNEXUS has empowered federal agencies and commercial enterprises to navigate the complexities of the digital landscape. As a quality-driven small business, we specialize in the seamless delivery of IT modernization and elite cybersecurity solutions. We help our clients modernize and fortify their technology stacks —ensuring their most critical data and assets remain resilient, optimized, and secure in an evolving threat environment.

Clearance:

Ability to obtain and maintain a Minimum Background Investigation (MBI) for our Department of Treasury customer. Candidates must reside in, and perform all work from, the continental United States or its outlying territories.

Location:

Remote (United States)

Work Schedule:

Full-time, remote. Must be available during core business hours (Eastern Time) to support scheduled audit activities. Travel to audited organization sites may be required on occasion, with advance notice.

Salary Range:

$115,000 to $140,000 annually, commensurate with experience

Position Overview:

AptNexus is seeking a Senior IT Security Auditor to perform cybersecurity compliance audits for our Department of Treasury customer. The program audits federal, state, and local government organizations that receive sensitive federal data, evaluating their information systems against security requirements tailored from NIST SP 800-53. In this role, you will plan and conduct audits of technical and management controls, perform hands-on configuration testing across operating systems, databases, network devices, cloud services, and mainframe platforms, and deliver clear, defensible findings to customer personnel and the audited organizations. The ideal candidate is a detail-oriented self-starter who combines disciplined audit practice with genuine technical depth.

Duties/Responsibilities:

  • Plan and conduct cybersecurity compliance audits of government partner organizations, establishing audit scope based on in-scope systems, data flows, and technologies.
  • Conduct pre-audit scoping calls to validate system inventories and data flows, and prepare scoping documentation identifying in-scope technologies, versions, support status, shared systems, applicable test procedures, and estimated level of effort.
  • Develop audit schedules and recommend auditor assignments that cover every in-scope technology while minimizing conflicts.
  • Perform hands-on technical control testing using automated scanning tools and manual configuration review against NIST SP 800-53 controls, CIS Benchmarks, and DISA STIGs.
  • Evaluate management controls through interviews with system administrators and examination of policies, procedures, and system artifacts.
  • Present audit scope and data flows at opening conferences, and present technical findings at closing conferences.
  • Provide daily written status updates during audits, including progress, outstanding work, potential critical findings, scope changes, and concerns.
  • Document test results and prepare preliminary findings, final audit report sections, and corrective action recommendations with risk-based remediation timelines.
  • Prepare after action reports capturing lessons learned and recommendations for process improvement.
  • Review the work of other auditors for accuracy and consistency, and provide technical guidance on complex testing and findings.
  • Educate audited organizations on applicable security requirements and recommended approaches to remediation.
  • Comply with all customer security, privacy, and records management requirements, using only Government-furnished equipment and approved systems.

Required Skills

  • Minimum of seven (7) years of cybersecurity experience, including at least five (5) years conducting federal cybersecurity audits or security control assessments.
  • Expert working knowledge of NIST SP 800-53 (moderate and high baselines), the NIST Risk Management Framework, NIST SP 800-30, and FIPS, including the ability to audit against control sets tailored from NIST.
  • Hands-on experience testing and validating security configurations on Windows, Linux, UNIX, and macOS systems; virtualization and container platforms (VMware, Hyper-V, Docker, Kubernetes, OpenShift); databases; and network devices such as firewalls, routers, switches, VPN, wireless, VoIP, and SAN/NAS storage.
  • Experience assessing cloud environments (AWS, Microsoft Azure and Microsoft 365, Google, Salesforce, and other FedRAMP-authorized services) across SaaS, IaaS, and PaaS service models.
  • Experience auditing mainframe security, including IBM RACF or ACF2, is strongly preferred.
  • Working knowledge of encryption technologies and standards, including TLS, VPN, and FIPS 140 validated cryptography.
  • Proficiency with automated scanning and compliance tools such as Tenable Nessus and SCAP, and with CIS Benchmarks and DISA STIGs.
  • Exceptional technical writing skills, with the ability to produce clear, well-supported, and defensible audit findings.
  • Advanced Microsoft Excel and Word skills; experience developing or using VBA macros is preferred.
  • Detail-oriented self-starter who takes ownership of assignments, manages competing priorities, and drives work to completion with minimal supervision.
  • Certification:
    • Must have at least one of the following certifications:
      • Certified Information Systems Auditor (CISA) (preferred)
      • CompTIA Cybersecurity Analyst (CySA+)
      • GIAC Systems and Network Auditor (GSNA)
  • Polished written and verbal communication skills, with the confidence to present findings to senior officials at audited organizations.
  • Sound professional judgment, objectivity, and integrity in handling sensitive information and audit results.
  • Must meet federal eligibility requirements for a position of public trust, including U.S. citizenship or lawful permanent residency, federal tax compliance, Selective Service registration (if applicable), a credit check, and fingerprinting.
  • Must complete customer-required security awareness training upon onboarding and annually thereafter.

Education Requirement:

High school diploma required. Bachelor’s degree in information technology, cybersecurity, information systems, accounting, or a related field preferred.

AptNexus is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability or protected veteran status.

Who We Are

We are a premier, accredited online language school seeking passionate Portuguese language instructors to join our team for the 2026-27 school year.

At LanguageBird, we believe meaningful learning happens through strong relationships, engaging instruction, and a commitment to continuous growth. We value educators who take initiative, bring positive energy to their work, and create supportive learning environments where students feel challenged, connected, and empowered to succeed.

We offer Middle School and High School Portuguese Levels 1–6+, as well as tutoring, conversational, and test-preparation courses.Our curriculum is ACTFL-aligned, and we are textbook-free.

raw.excerpt: Who are we? Applied AI for liquidity. Corporate finance teams still manage cash by hand — stitching together spreadsheets, bank portals and ERP data across Treasury, AR and AP.
raw.description:
Who are we?

Applied AI for liquidity.

Corporate finance teams still manage cash by hand — stitching together spreadsheets, bank portals and ERP data across Treasury, AR and AP. Most treasury tools stop at visibility: a dashboard someone still has to read, interpret and act on.

Nilus goes further. We're building an agentic workforce for treasury — AI agents that reconcile cash, forecast liquidity and automate finance ops across every bank and ERP, in one connected system for Treasury, AR and AP.

We're a Series A company backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, Felicis, Perpetual Growth and Better Tomorrow Ventures, led by a team of ex-fintech pros transforming the finance function.

The role

Nilus is hiring an FDE to sit between our customers and our product. You'll work directly with treasury and finance teams to understand how they really run cash. You'll turn that into solutions on the Nilus platform and bring what you learn back to Product and R&D so it shapes what we build next.

This role is for someone who understands treasury and thinks like a product person. You know how cash positioning, forecasting, bank reconciliation and payments fit together. You're just as comfortable designing a workflow with a customer's treasurer as you are writing requirements with a product manager.

You'll be customer-facing across the lifecycle: early solution design, rollout, adoption and expansion. You'll also be one of the strongest voices of the customer inside the company.

What you'll do

  • Run deep discovery with customers and prospects to map their treasury workflows, data sources and banking setup, and design how Nilus solves them.
  • Own solution design for new customers, from scoping integrations and bank connectivity to configuring forecasting, reconciliation and reporting to fit their processes.
  • Design and refine the agent workflows customers run on Nilus, and turn customer-specific solutions into repeatable product patterns.
  • Translate customer needs into clear product requirements, and work with Product and R&D (Tel Aviv) on prioritization, specs and validation.
  • Run beta and early-access programs for new features: pick design partners, collect feedback, and confirm the feature solves the problem before general release.
  • Support pre-sales when deals need product depth: solution workshops, technical deep dives and tailored demos alongside Sales.
  • Partner with Customer Success on rollouts and adoption, and spot expansion opportunities based on how customers use the product.
  • Create solution guides, use-case libraries and enablement content for Sales, CS and Marketing.
  • Track how treasury teams, TMS platforms and competitors are evolving, and feed that into product strategy.

What we're looking for

  • 5+ years in corporate treasury, treasury consulting, or an FDE / product / solutions role at a fintech or TMS company
  • Hands-on product experience, such as product management, product operations, or solutions work closely tied to a product roadmap
  • Strong grasp of cash management workflows, banking data structures (BAI2, MT940, APIs) and reconciliation processes
  • Familiarity with SaaS-based treasury management (TMS) or cash management platforms
  • Proven customer-facing experience with finance and treasury leaders, from analysts to CFOs
  • Comfortable with APIs, data mapping and system integrations (you won't be coding, but you'll design and scope the solution)
  • Ability to write clear product requirements and turn messy customer input into structured priorities
  • Hands-on interest in AI agents and how they change finance workflows
  • Self-starter who thrives in a fast-paced, ambiguous startup environment
  • NYC-based or able to work US hours

Nilus is an equal opportunity employer. We consider all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.
